summary: Intent design for security-center-event-observation-panel-v1 from design/tasks/security-center-event-observation-panel-v1.md. Security Center must add a V1 operator observation panel on top of the existing Security Event Ingestion V1 records: one default 24-hour page with quick ranges for 1 hour, 24 hours, and 7 days; summary statistics over legal accepted events; a HIGH/MEDIUM alert list; a raw reception list that includes both successful events and failed reception records; and alert-to-raw evidence traceability. V1 remains an observation panel, not a disposition, ticketing, assignment, approval, risk scoring, custom analytics, raw-payload full-text search, raw-payload export, requester identity, or authentication platform.

explicitTestcases.name: security-center-event-observation-panel-v1-posture-statistics
explicitTestcases.controlPoint: Submit five legal accepted security events inside the selected time range, covering multiple sourceSystem values, multiple eventTypeId values, and multiple severity values, with exactly two HIGH events; then open the observation panel for that range.
explicitTestcases.observationPoint: The summary area shows total accepted event count 5, HIGH accepted event count 2, and sourceSystem and eventTypeId distributions exactly matching the submitted accepted events.
explicitTestcases.acceptanceBoundary: tests/e2e/security_center/test_security_event_observation_panel.py::test_observation_panel_summarizes_current_event_posture must be materialized by Implementation Design as the explicit entrypoint for observation-panel posture statistics.
explicitTestcases.implementationNotes: The statistic source of truth is accepted legal Security Event records in the selected range. Failed reception records are raw evidence only and must not increase legal event counts or distributions.

explicitTestcases.name: security-center-event-observation-panel-v1-alert-scope
explicitTestcases.controlPoint: Submit one DEBUG, one LOW, one MEDIUM, and one HIGH legal accepted event inside the selected time range; then open the observation panel.
explicitTestcases.observationPoint: The alert list shows only the MEDIUM and HIGH accepted events, while the raw reception list shows all four successful reception records.
explicitTestcases.acceptanceBoundary: tests/e2e/security_center/test_security_event_observation_panel.py::test_observation_panel_filters_alerts_by_severity must be materialized by Implementation Design as the explicit entrypoint for alert-list severity scope.
explicitTestcases.implementationNotes: HIGH and MEDIUM accepted events are alert-focus rows. LOW and DEBUG are not alerts in V1, but they remain successful raw reception rows.

explicitTestcases.name: security-center-event-observation-panel-v1-alert-ordering
explicitTestcases.controlPoint: Submit multiple HIGH and MEDIUM legal accepted events with interleaved occurredAt timestamps inside the selected time range; then open the observation panel alert list.
explicitTestcases.observationPoint: All HIGH alerts appear before all MEDIUM alerts, and alerts with the same severity are ordered by occurredAt descending.
explicitTestcases.acceptanceBoundary: tests/e2e/security_center/test_security_event_observation_panel.py::test_observation_panel_sorts_alerts_by_severity_and_occurred_at must be materialized by Implementation Design as the explicit entrypoint for alert ordering.
explicitTestcases.implementationNotes: Alert ordering is severity priority first, then occurredAt descending. receivedAt ordering from the older inbox list must not override this panel-specific alert ordering.

explicitTestcases.name: security-center-event-observation-panel-v1-failed-receptions-visible
explicitTestcases.controlPoint: Submit invalid events for an illegal source, a missing required field, and a payload type error inside the selected time range; then open the observation panel raw reception list.
explicitTestcases.observationPoint: The failed reception records do not increase legal event summary counts and do not appear in the alert list, but they appear in the raw reception list with failure reason and bounded raw-payload summary.
explicitTestcases.acceptanceBoundary: tests/e2e/security_center/test_security_event_observation_panel.py::test_observation_panel_shows_failed_receptions_in_raw_records must be materialized by Implementation Design as the explicit entrypoint for failed reception visibility.
explicitTestcases.implementationNotes: Use the existing Security Event Failure Record semantics from sec-event-ingestion-v1. This testcase freezes raw-list visibility and non-pollution of stats/alerts, not a new retention promise.

explicitTestcases.name: security-center-event-observation-panel-v1-alert-to-raw-traceability
explicitTestcases.controlPoint: Submit one HIGH legal accepted event, open the observation panel, and select that event in the alert list.
explicitTestcases.observationPoint: The raw reception list locates or filters to the same sourceSystem plus eventId raw record, and the operator can open or view the bounded raw payload evidence for that record.
explicitTestcases.acceptanceBoundary: tests/e2e/security_center/test_security_event_observation_panel.py::test_observation_panel_links_alert_to_raw_record must be materialized by Implementation Design as the explicit entrypoint for alert-to-raw traceability.
explicitTestcases.implementationNotes: The requirement allows locating or filtering. Recommended Implementation Design choice is to freeze a filtered/focused raw-list state keyed by sourceSystem plus eventId because it is deterministic for tests and preserves evidence traceability.

explicitTestcases.name: security-center-event-observation-panel-v1-time-range-consistency
explicitTestcases.controlPoint: Construct accepted and failed reception records inside the latest 1 hour, inside the latest 24 hours, inside the latest 7 days, and outside the latest 7 days; then switch the panel among latest 1 hour, latest 24 hours, and latest 7 days.
explicitTestcases.observationPoint: After each quick-range change, the summary area, alert list, and raw reception list all include only records within the same selected range and do not contradict each other.
explicitTestcases.acceptanceBoundary: tests/e2e/security_center/test_security_event_observation_panel.py::test_observation_panel_applies_time_range_consistently must be materialized by Implementation Design as the explicit entrypoint for shared time-range interpretation.
explicitTestcases.implementationNotes: Default range is latest 24 hours. Implementation Design must define stable clock control or fixture data construction so 1h/24h/7d boundaries are executable without flaky wall-clock assumptions.

openQuestions.question: Should selecting an alert locate the raw row in-place or filter the raw reception list to only the same sourceSystem plus eventId?
openQuestions.recommendedAnswer: Use a deterministic filtered or focused raw-list state keyed by sourceSystem plus eventId, while allowing the UI to visually highlight the row when practical.
openQuestions.reason: The requirement permits locate or filter. Freezing the sourceSystem plus eventId filtered/focused observation makes the acceptance test stable while preserving the product goal of tracing alert evidence.

openQuestions.question: Should the observation panel introduce automatic alerting, disposition status, ticketing, assignment, comments, approval, risk scoring, custom reports, full-text raw-payload search, raw-payload export, requester identity, or request authentication?
openQuestions.recommendedAnswer: No. Keep V1 as an observation and evidence-traceability panel only.
openQuestions.reason: Both the source task and the underlying Security Event Ingestion V1 PRD explicitly exclude those product commitments. Adding them would redesign intent beyond this task.

notes: This handoff intentionally builds on existing sec-event-ingestion-v1 accepted event and failed reception semantics rather than redefining ingestion, validation, idempotency, durable persistence, failure-record bounding, or Web detail behavior.

Implementation Design must update root and local architecture contracts so deploy/api owns any panel read-model/API needed for shared time range, summary statistics, alert ordering, raw reception records, and alert-to-raw lookup; deploy/web owns the operator panel rendering and interactions by consuming deploy/api only.

Implementation Design must materialize executable explicit Web acceptance entrypoints under tests/e2e/security_center/test_security_event_observation_panel.py and should use tests/integration/security/security_event_harness.py for business-readable seeding and observation helpers.

Implementation Design must produce design/KG/ImplementationToCodingHandoff.json and design/KG/test-failure-records.json after materializing executable entrypoints. Expected initial failures are acceptable if production behavior is not yet implemented, but placeholder passing tests are not acceptable.
